subject: Uptime credit math & maintenance window scheduling - order form redlines
messages:

Cc: NovaCorp Contracts <support-contracts@novacorp.com>

Subject: Order form QA: uptime credit calc + maintenance windows

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for sending the latest Order Form. Our legal and SRE teams ran a quick pass and have two areas that need clearer language before procurement can move to signature: the service-credit calculation for partial-month availability hits, and the boundaries for maintenance windows (especially how rolling maintenance vs. blackout maintenance are treated).

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm the exact formula Redwood is using to compute service credits when monthly availability falls between the defined buckets? Our SRE would like an explicit example with numbers.
- We need a clearer carve-out for planned multi-region maintenance that NovaCorp may designate as a business-critical blackout (we would propose a maximum of 2 ad-hoc blackout days per quarter).

Procurement is targeting a final counter-signature by 2028-07-20, so any redlines that affect credit math/maintenance definitions will need to be resolved this week.

Appreciate the help.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Cloud Ops
NovaCorp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 10:03:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form QA: uptime credit calc + maintenance windows

Hi Elena — thanks for the notes. Looping in Laura (contracts) and Kimberly (SRE/product) to align on precise language.

Short answers up front:
- Formula: Redwood proposes a pro-rata credit that scales linearly between slate thresholds. See the attached uptime-credit-excel.xlsx for three numeric examples (full month = 720 hours baseline; credits expressed as % of monthly fee). Example excerpt: if Availability = 98.2% (13.0 hours downtime in month), Credit = ((99.9 - 98.2) / (99.9 - 99.0)) * 10% = 18.89% of monthly fee, capped at 100% of monthly fee.
- Maintenance: we accept a defined blackout carve-out but need to limit ad-hoc blackouts to preserve platform reliability; propose language that allows up to 2 blackout days/quarter with at least 72h prior notice for each, and allows Redwood-initiated emergency maintenance with notification and escalation credits.

I attached a redline of the Order Form (NC_OrderForm_v3-redline.pdf) with inline edits to the credit formula (paragraph 4.2) and the maintenance carve-outs (paragraphs 6.1-6.3).

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync at 3pm PT today to walk numbers and align final wording. If that doesn't work, we can do first thing Monday.

Thanks,
Rishi
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- NC_OrderForm_v3-redline.pdf (PDF, 183 KB)
- uptime-credit-excel.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 11:45:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form QA: uptime credit calc + maintenance windows

Internal — do not forward until legal has redlined.

Rishi / Kim, quick take after reading Rishi's redline:

1) Credit computation: the linear interpolation approach is fine, but legal will want explicit caps and a tie-back to how "monthly fee" is defined (billing period vs. invoice period). I propose the following clause addition under 4.2: 

   "For partial-month credits, Redwood will compute Credits by linear interpolation between the next-higher Availability bucket and the next-lower bucket as set forth in Table A. 'Monthly Fee' shall mean the portion of the customer's recurring subscription fee invoiced for the applicable billing period (excluding usage-based charges). Credits are not cumulative and shall be applied against future invoices."

2) Maintenance carve-outs: instead of fixed calendar days per quarter, what about a quota measured in total blackout hours per rolling 90-day window (e.g., 48 hours/rolling 90-day period) with a separate clause for business-critical blackouts that require a named exec approval from NovaCorp? This gives us operational flexibility and a precise cap.

3) Emergency maintenance: add automatic escalation to our 24x7 on-call and a partial credit if Redwood fails to notify within the agreed SLA window.

Action items: can we (a) get legal to redline the attached PDF with the "Monthly Fee" definition and the rolling-hours wording, and (b) have Kim provide a short statement on operational impact of a customer-designated blackout (one paragraph) to include in the SOW?

Thanks — I'll flag this for legal once we agree internally.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novacorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaCorp Contracts <support-contracts@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 15:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form QA: uptime credit calc + maintenance windows

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround and the worked examples. We can accept Redwood's linear interpolation approach if two changes are made:

1) Add explicit language that customer-designated blackout days (the ones NovaCorp flags as business-critical) are excluded from the calculation but limited to a maximum of 16 hours per quarter per region (not days). Our ops team needs the regional carveout so we can coordinate heavy batch jobs.
2) For rolling blackout hours, NovaCorp requests that any usage of the blackout allowance that would push the rolling window over 48 hours triggers a mandatory operational review and a capped credit equal to 5% of the monthly fee for that month as a mitigation.

If we can get those two items in writing and an example in the Order Form redline, procurement will expedite approval. We remain on track for 2028-07-20 signature provided the redlines are incorporated and legal approves.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Cloud Ops
NovaCorp
